Mina — thanks again for the demo Friday. Our leadership liked the latency and the cost estimates, and we'd like to move forward with a short POC. Before we lock dates, can you confirm the MAP items we need to close on our side so infra can schedule work? Specifically: 
- Org setup and tenant provisioning (who on your side creates the org & invites)
- API key issuance and scoping (ephemeral vs long-lived for testing)
- IP allowlist ranges for initial staging / test runs
- VPC peering window and expected lead time

We are targeting a 2-week window in mid-Apr to run a 3-day load sweep. Can you send a checklist and the earliest possible dates for preflight checks? I'm including our DevOps alias for timeline coordination.

Thanks,
Amit

MediSprint

Amit — really appreciate the clear ask. Below is a compact MAP-oriented checklist and our proposed preflight dates. I'm copying Neha (security) and Evelyn (onboarding ops) to confirm internal owners.

High-level MAP checklist (what we will deliver / what we need from MediSprint):
- Redwood will: create a sandbox org, invite two owners (RBAC: org-admin + billing-contact)
  - MediSprint action: confirm the two invite e-mails + preferred org slug
- API keys: we will issue an ephemeral test key and a scoped long-lived key for the POC (read/limited-write)
  - MediSprint action: confirm SRV IPs that should be able to call the endpoints (we'll use IP allowlist + token binding)
- IP allowlist: provide two CIDR blocks for staging; we will pre-seed the allowlist and do a connectivity smoke test
  - MediSprint action: hand off the CIDRs and any NAT/GW info by EOD Apr 6
- VPC peering: we support AWS VPC peering (cross-account) or PrivateLink depending on your infra. Typical lead time is 5 business days after we exchange account IDs and route tables.
  - MediSprint action: confirm preference (peering vs PrivateLink) and share account ID/route table by Apr 6

Proposed calendar for preflight & POC: 
- Apr 6: MediSprint provides org slug, two invite emails, CIDR blocks, account IDs (deadline)
- Apr 7-9: Redwood provisions sandbox org, issues ephemeral test key, seeds IP allowlist, initial smoke test (no traffic)
- Apr 10: VPC peering handshake initiated; both sides validate routes
- Apr 12-14: POC traffic window (3-day sweep)

Deliverables I'll attach: preflight checklist, VPC peering diagram, and a minimal test plan. Can Neha confirm the token binding approach below? Evelyn — can you capture the provisioning steps and confirm any rate-limit guardrails for the POC?

Thanks — I'll send a calendar invite once we have the CIDRs.

Best,
Mina
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Mina / Amit — quick security confirmation and a short checklist from my side. We will: 
1) Issue two API key types for POC:
   - Ephemeral test key (TTL 24 hrs) for initial integration and smoke tests
   - Scoped long-lived key for load runs (scoped to the POC org & usage limits)
2) Enforce token binding to IPs you provide (CIDRs) and optional TLS client-auth if you prefer
3) Audit logs: we will enable request-level logging for the POC (retained for 30 days by default)
4) ACLs & routing: we need the exact route table IDs and the AWS account ID for peering; please redact any sensitive fields in email, use secure drop (I've shared a temporary S3 bucket link in the notes below)

Security asks for MediSprint (action items):
- Provide two invite emails (org-admin + billing)
- Provide two CIDR blocks for staging (example: 10.4.0.0/24, 35.181.0.0/24)
- Share AWS account ID and route table IDs (or confirm PrivateLink preference) via secure channel

Notes & links: 
- Secure upload: https://redwood-secure.example/s3/temp-drop/RWINF-3421 (expires in 7d)
- Minimal POC logging policy: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/POC-logging-policy

I'll approve the scoped long-lived key once we have the CIDRs and account ID. Evelyn, can you confirm who will run the smoke test and whether we need an internal runbook entry?

-Neha
Director, InfoSec | Redwood Inference

- DevOps (cc) prefers VPC peering; I'll ask them to confirm the precise route table IDs in their upload.
